cues.en: he averaged over all random codes and showed the average was arbitrarily good. Therefore, one good code had to exist.
cues.zh: 他对所有随机码取平均，并证明这个平均值可以任意好。因此，一定存在一种好码。

cues.en: Who but a man with almost infinite courage would do that?
cues.zh: 除了一个有近乎无限勇气的人，谁会这么做？

cues.en: He had it. Now I can tell you another way simply.
cues.zh: 他就有这种勇气。现在我可以简单用另一种方式讲。

cues.en: There was a year or so when he came in about 10:00, played chess till about two and went home.
cues.zh: 有大约一年时间，他十点左右来，下棋到两点左右，然后回家。

cues.en: At the end of the year, the company gave him a salary raise. That's all you could see him doing was that at home he was creating information to him. Well, the way he played chess
cues.zh: 年底，公司给他加了薪。你所能看到他在做的就只有这些，而他在家里其实是在创建信息论。嗯，他下棋的方式

cues.en: is the following.
cues.zh: 是这样的。

cues.en: When you are attacking chess, you can either defend yourself or you can attack back.
cues.zh: 当你在下国际象棋时，你可以防守，也可以反击。

cues.en: Shannon never defended himself.
cues.zh: Shannon 从不防守。

cues.en: He attacked back.
cues.zh: 他会反击。

cues.en: And the game would get tied up more and more and more and more complex.
cues.zh: 然后局势会变得越来越复杂、越来越复杂。

cues.en: And finally, stop and think for a long while, grab his queen and advance and say, I'm scared not.
cues.zh: 最后，他会停下来思考好久，抓起他的王后向前一步，说：“我才不怕呢。”

cues.en: Bingo. The whole game would collapse then because he finally precipitated all the pending operations and either won or lost.
cues.zh: 太妙了。整个棋局随后就会崩溃，因为他终于集中触发了所有挂起的操作，要么赢，要么输。

cues.en: Well, I learned that expression. I ain't scared nothing.
cues.zh: 好吧，我学到了这句话：我什么都不怕。

cues.en: I've used this several times on myself. When stuck, I didn't know what on earth to do. I said, good
cues.zh: 我曾在自己身上多次用过这招。当卡壳时，我真不知道该怎么办才好。我说：

cues.en: enough for Shen, good enough for Heming. I ain't scared nothing. Let's go ahead and see what happens.
cues.zh: 对 Shen 适用，对 Heming 也适用。我什么都不怕。放手一搏，看看到底会发生什么。

cues.en: And sometimes,
cues.zh: 有时，

cues.en: by copying his style, I came through to success.
cues.zh: 通过模仿他的风格，我走向了成功。

cues.en: I deliberately copied his style.
cues.zh: 我有意模仿了他的风格。

cues.en: Now another example.
cues.zh: 现在来看另一个例子。

cues.en: I hope most people are dead. I guess they aren't, but they won't hear this.
cues.zh: 我希望大多数人已经不在了。我猜他们不在，不过他们也听不到这个。

cues.en: I
cues.zh: 我

cues.en: was in a math department and the math department,
cues.zh: 曾在数学系，而在数学系里，

cues.en: we used to go to lunch together. They played games through boomerangs, flew kites, and played this and that.
cues.zh: 我们过去常常一起吃午饭。他们玩飞旋镖、放风筝、玩各种游戏。

cues.en: And they fiddled around. And I
cues.zh: 他们无所事事。而我

cues.en: wanted to succeed and I said I can't afford to waste lunch times. So I went around to the physics table where I'd written a paper with one of physicists,
cues.zh: 渴望成功，我说我可浪费不起午休时间。于是我转到了物理系的那张桌子，我曾和其中一位物理学家合写过一篇论文，

cues.en: a good one. I said, may I join you? Sure. I'm welcome.
cues.zh: 一个很厉害的物理学家。我说：“我能加入你们吗？”“当然可以。”我很受欢迎。

cues.en: The table consists among other people of Bardeen, Shockley, Bratton, the Nobel Prize winners, JB Johnson, Johnson Noyes, and some others, my friend.
cues.zh: 这张桌子上的其他人包括诺贝尔奖得主 Bardeen、Shockley、Bratton，还有 JB Johnson、Johnson Noyes 以及一些其他人，我的朋友。

cues.en: And
cues.zh: 还有

cues.en: I used to have lunch with him for years.
cues.zh: 我曾经和他一起吃了好几年的午饭。

cues.en: I learned a lot. I learned a lot of tricks out of Shockley, how he did things. I watched other people. I learned how to do things sensibly.
cues.zh: 我学到了很多，学到了很多从肖克利那里学来的窍门，知道他是怎么做事的。我也观察其他人，学会了如何明智地做事。

cues.en: Well, finally, the Nobel Prize came through, promotion came through, jobs elsewhere came through,
cues.zh: 后来，诺贝尔奖颁下来了，晋升也实现了，其他地方的工作机会也来了，

cues.en: and all the able people left,
cues.zh: 于是所有有能力的人都离开了，

cues.en: including my friend. He had promoted up the line.
cues.zh: 包括我的朋友。他一路晋升了上去。

cues.en: Well, what was left
cues.zh: 那么，剩下的

cues.en: was the Drakes,
cues.zh: 就是那些德雷克斯，

cues.en: hardly worth eating lunch with.
cues.zh: 几乎不值得一起吃午饭。

cues.en: Well, over in the other corner of the dining room was a big table,
cues.zh: 餐厅的另一个角落有一张大桌子，

cues.en: And I had written a paper on nuclear bag gag resins with one of the guys.
cues.zh: 我曾和其中一个人写过一篇关于核袋胶树脂的论文。

cues.en: And so I said, do you mind if I join you? So I sit down and we talked about chemistry
cues.zh: 于是我说，你介意我加入你们吗？我坐下来后，我们聊起了化学

cues.en: and such other things for a long while.
cues.zh: 以及其他类似的事情，聊了很久。

cues.en: And finally,
cues.zh: 最后，

cues.en: one day,
cues.zh: 有一天，

cues.en: I walk in and say, if what you're working on is not important
cues.zh: 我走进去说，如果你们正在做的事情并不重要，

cues.en: and it's not likely to lead to important things,
cues.zh: 也不太可能带来什么重要成果，

cues.en: why are you working on it?
cues.zh: 那你们为什么还要做呢？

cues.en: After that, I ate with the engineers.
cues.zh: 从那以后，我就和工程师们一起吃饭。

cues.en: That was spring. In the fall, going down the long corridor Bell Labs,
cues.zh: 那是春天。秋天时，我沿着贝尔实验室的长走廊走着，

cues.en: my friend chemist stopped me and said, you know, Hamming, that remarkable year has got underneath my skin.
cues.zh: 我的化学家朋友拦住我说：“你知道吗，汉明，那非凡的一年已经让我念念不忘。”

cues.en: I've spent the summer thinking about the important problems in my field. I have not changed my research, but I think it was well worth the time.
cues.zh: 整个夏天，我都在思考自己领域里的重要问题。我没有改变研究方向，但我觉得花这些时间非常值得。

cues.en: I say thank you Dave and walk on.
cues.zh: 我说了声谢谢，戴夫，然后继续往前走。

cues.en: About two weeks later, I noticed he's made head of the department.
cues.zh: 大约两周后，我注意到他已经成了系主任。

cues.en: About ten or twelve years ago, I noticed he is a member of National Academy of Engineering.
cues.zh: 大约十到十二年后，我注意到他成了美国国家工程院院士。

cues.en: I have never heard of anything about any other person at chemistry table.
cues.zh: 我从未听说过化学桌旁其他任何人的任何事。

cues.en: Not one.
cues.zh: 一个都没有。

cues.en: The one man who could hear,
cues.zh: 那个能听进去的人，

cues.en: if what you're doing is not important, not likely important, why are you doing it? The one man who could
cues.zh: 如果你做的事不重要，也不太可能重要，那你为什么还要做？那个能够

cues.en: did become important.
cues.zh: 确实变得重要了。

cues.en: He did succeed.
cues.zh: 他确实成功了。

cues.en: The rest of them who couldn't hear didn't.
cues.zh: 其余听不进去的人则没有。

cues.en: It's that simple.
cues.zh: 就这么简单。

cues.en: If you don't work on important problems, you are not going to do important things except by the dumbest of dumb luck.
cues.zh: 如果你不研究重要问题，就不可能做出重要的事，除非你撞上最蠢的运气。

cues.en: You must work on important problems. Now you can't work on them all the time because that's what Nobel Prize winners do.
cues.zh: 你必须研究重要问题。但你不能一直只研究它们，因为诺贝尔奖得主才会那样。

cues.en: They get a Nobel Prize and they think like Shannon also. They can only work on important problems.
cues.zh: 他们得了诺贝尔奖，也像 Shannon 那样想。他们只能研究重要问题。

cues.en: As a result, they don't do anything.
cues.zh: 结果，他们什么也做不成。

cues.en: You have to plant little acorns which grow into my oak trees.
cues.zh: 你得种下小橡子，让它们长成我的橡树。

cues.en: But you have to plant the acorns which will grow.
cues.zh: 但你必须种下能长大的橡子。

cues.en: You have to learn the small things. So the great thing
cues.zh: 你得学会小事。所以，最大的

cues.en: thing wrong with Nobel Prizes is you now think you've only worked on important problems.
cues.zh: 诺贝尔奖的问题在于，你现在以为自己只研究过重要问题。

cues.en: And you don't. What you have to work on are problems which can become important and matter,
cues.zh: 其实你并没有。你必须研究的是那些可能变得重要、有意义的问题，

cues.en: which have a future,
cues.zh: 有前途的问题，

cues.en: which will grow into mighty oak trees.
cues.zh: 能长成参天橡树的问题。

cues.en: Another thing that ruins Nobel Prize winner, of course, is everybody
cues.zh: 当然，毁掉诺贝尔奖得主的另一件事，就是每个人

cues.en: gets famous. Are put in all kinds of committees, all kinds of other things, and you can't get any work done.
cues.zh: 都出名了。被安排进各种委员会、各种其他事务，结果你什么工作都做不成。

cues.en: They stop you from doing it
cues.zh: 他们会阻止你做研究

cues.en: by various promotions and so on. So that's a lot of reasons why Nobel Prize winners often don't do very much afterwards.
cues.zh: 用各种晋升之类的方式。所以，诺贝尔奖得主之后往往做不出什么成果，原因有很多。

cues.en: Now confidence in yourself, I said, is important. Overconfidence, of course, is a disaster.
cues.zh: 我曾经说过，自信是很重要的。当然，过度的自信就是一场灾难。

cues.en: I'll put as... As I did the other day, the difference between being strong willed and stubborn.
cues.zh: 我用……就像我前几天说的那样，来区分意志坚定和固执。

cues.en: Remembering confidence and overconfidence about the same thing. It's this fine line. I've seen a lot of people abandon a good idea too soon,
cues.zh: 记住，自信和过度自信往往一线之隔。这是一条很微妙的界限。我见过很多人过早地放弃了一个好主意，

cues.en: and I've seen people cling to a bad idea too long.
cues.zh: 我也见过有人在一个烂主意上死缠烂打太久。

cues.en: They're both difficult problems.
cues.zh: 这两个都是棘手的问题。

cues.en: Now one of the features which you can cling to regularly
cues.zh: 现在，你可以长期坚持的特征之一，

cues.en: is a desire to do excellent work.
cues.zh: 就是对精益求精的渴望。

cues.en: Whatever you do, you're going to do well.
cues.zh: 无论你做什么，都要把它做好。

cues.en: Now it's not true. My father said, anything worth doing all is worth doing well. There are some things you might as well get rid of.
cues.zh: 但这其实不对。我父亲说过，任何值得做的事都值得做好。有些事你最好赶紧应付过去。

cues.en: Like you have to sign some paper for this or that. You just sign them. You don't try and write your handwriting the most beautiful one you can. You just get rid of it. But in general, you try and do excellence. There's a one guide I think you can say whatever I do I am going to do well.
cues.zh: 比如你得签这文件那文件的。签了就完事。你不用刻意去写最漂亮的签名。赶紧应付完就行。但总的来说，你要追求卓越。我认为有一个准则你可以遵循：无论做什么，我都要做到最好。

cues.en: And that will give you some unity because I've talked to you before about the drunken sailor who staggered a couple steps this way, a couple this way, a couple this way. In a total of many, many steps, he gets a distance to square root of n.
cues.zh: 这会给你带来一些凝聚力，因为我以前跟你讲过那个醉水手的故事，他东倒西歪地迈出几步，又往那边走几步，再往那边走几步。在总共迈出许许多多的步子后，他前进的距离正比于步数的平方根。

cues.en: But if there's a pretty girl over there, he sags like this, he sags like this, and he gets a distance proportional to n. When you have a vision,
cues.zh: 但如果那边有个漂亮的姑娘，他就会朝着那个方向歪歪扭扭地走过去，他前进的距离就会与步数成正比。当你有了愿景，

cues.en: you will go a long way. Without a vision of what you're going to do and where you're going to be,
cues.zh: 你就会走得很远。如果没有对要做的事情和未来的方向有清晰的愿景，

cues.en: you're not going to get very far.
cues.zh: 你是走不了多远的。

cues.en: It's that simple.
cues.zh: 就是这么简单。

cues.en: You have to get a vision of what you are going to do and be and then pursue it. Excellence is one of the best tracks you could use. I'm going to do things very well. I'm going to do more than just a good job. I'm going to a first class job.
cues.zh: 你必须对你想做什么、想成为什么样的人有清晰的愿景，然后去追求它。追求卓越是你可以选择的最好路径之一。我要把事情做到极致。我不仅仅要做好一份工作，我要做到一流。

cues.en: Now what you may consider good working conditions may not be for you. It's very sad, but what you think are good working conditions are not.
cues.zh: 现在，你认为好的工作环境对你来说可能并不好。这很悲哀，但你以为的好工作环境其实不然。

cues.en: The example I've given you already is working with a door closed or opener. If you work with a door closed,
cues.zh: 我刚才举的例子是关着门工作还是开着门工作。如果你关着门工作，

cues.en: you won't be interrupted. You get your work done.
cues.zh: 你就不会被打扰。你能完成工作。

cues.en: You work with a door open, people come by and stop and chat and so on and so on.
cues.zh: 如果你开着门工作，人们会走过来停下聊天，诸如此类。

cues.en: But I've noticed very clearly at Bell Laboratories,
cues.zh: 但我注意到在贝尔实验室，

cues.en: those who work with the door shut
cues.zh: 那些关着门工作的人，

cues.en: may be working just as hard ten years later, but they don't know what to work on. They are not connected with reality.
cues.zh: 十年后可能依然工作得一样努力，但他们却不知道该做什么。他们与现实脱节了。

cues.en: Those who had the door open may very well know what's important.
cues.zh: 而那些开着门的人，则很清楚什么才是重要的。

cues.en: Now I cannot prove to you whether the open door causes the open mind or whether the open mind causes the open door. I suspect
cues.zh: 现在我无法向你证明，是开着门导致了开放的心态，还是开放的心态导致了开着门。我怀疑

cues.en: suspect a pill. I can only establish the correlation.
cues.zh: ……我只能证实它们之间存在相关性。

cues.en: And it was quite spectacular.
cues.zh: 而且这相当惊人。

cues.en: Almost always.
cues.zh: 几乎总是如此。

cues.en: The guy with the door closed were often very well able, very gifted, but they seem to work always on slightly the wrong problem.
cues.zh: 关着门的那家伙通常能力很强、非常有天赋，但他们似乎总在稍微错误的问题上钻研。

cues.en: So you have to get wide feeling for what is going on.
cues.zh: 所以你必须对正在发生的事情有广泛的感知。

cues.en: And the supreme example of this closure is the Institute for Advanced Study in Princeton.
cues.zh: 这种闭包的最佳例子就是普林斯顿高等研究院。

cues.en: They take in people who've done something great. They give them luxury, a beautiful office, a beautiful restaurant and dine in, a wonderful grounds and everything else like that, adequate salary to live on, no cares, no worries, no nothing. You're freed for life or anything at all.
cues.zh: 他们招揽那些已经做出伟大成就的人。给他们奢华待遇，漂亮的办公室，漂亮的餐厅还能在里面用餐，优美的园区等等，薪水足够生活，无忧无虑，什么都不用操心。你这辈子就自由了，想干什么都行。

cues.en: What happens? The Balkan continue working on the problem they made... That made them famous. They keep on elaborating and so on. They've
cues.zh: 结果呢？这些人继续钻研让他们成名的那个问题。他们不断深化拓展之类的。他们已经

cues.en: already made it famous. It doesn't have to be added to. They got the thing going.
cues.zh: 让它出名了。不需要再添砖加瓦了。他们已经把东西做起来了。

cues.en: Rarely do they change. Now Von Neumann was first different. He was the institute and he did go out in reality and turn up in Washington and other places. He traveled widely and was receptive to new ideas.
cues.zh: 很少有人会改变。冯·诺依曼是第一个例外。他属于研究院，但他确实走出去，出现在华盛顿和其他地方。他到处旅行，乐于接受新想法。

cues.en: But the bulk of the people who got appointed institute for advanced study
cues.zh: 但被任命到高等研究院的大多数人

cues.en: don't keep the door open on life as it were, and they don't do anything comparable to what they had done before. They are very able people,
cues.zh: 可以说并不对生活敞开大门，他们也不会做出跟之前相当的成就。他们都是非常有能力的人，

cues.en: but the institute, in my opinion, sterilize them to a great extent.
cues.zh: 但在我看来，研究院在很大程度上把他们给 sterilize 了。

cues.en: So what do you think is the ideal working conditions or not?
cues.zh: 那你觉得理想的工作条件是什么，还是说不是？

cues.en: Now, I'll give you some examples
cues.zh: 我给你们举几个例子

cues.en: of this.
cues.zh: 关于这个。

cues.en: When we began with the IBM seven zero one computer, we programmed in absolute binary. And there were a bunch of these machines in the West Coast airframe companies and the rest were scattered around.
cues.zh: 我们开始用 IBM 701 计算机的时候，编程用的是绝对二进制。西海岸的机身制造公司里有一批这种机器，其余的分散在各地。

cues.en: Now it became obvious to me that the method the West Coast used for programming, namely, we hire an acre of girls spread out and they program.
cues.zh: 这时候我突然意识到，西海岸那边采用的编程方法是，我们雇一大片女程序员，分散开来让她们写程序。

cues.en: Typically girls, but sometimes men, but mainly they were programming girls in those days.
cues.zh: 通常是女孩子，有时也有男的，但那年头主要都是女程序员。

cues.en: Well, was clear to me Bell Labs would never give me an acre of girls.
cues.zh: 好吧，我很清楚贝尔实验室绝不可能给我分配一大片女程序员。

cues.en: They weren't about to do that kind of a thing.
cues.zh: 他们才不会搞那种事情。

cues.en: Well, what do I do? I mean, computing. I wanna be in the frontier.
cues.zh: 那我要怎么办？我是说，关于计算。我想站在技术的前沿。

cues.en: What everybody else has, I'm not gonna have.
cues.zh: 别人都有的资源，我是不会有了。

cues.en: Well, I could quit getting job on the West Coast.
cues.zh: 好吧，我可以辞职去西海岸找工作。

cues.en: Probably anyone in a number of airframes companies because I was wheezing me no one out there.
cues.zh: 随便去哪家飞机制造公司都行，因为当时我在那边也算小有名气。

cues.en: But Bell Labs had a lot of very good people and the airframe companies have a few good people scattered widely,
cues.zh: 但贝尔实验室有很多非常优秀的人，而飞机制造公司只有少数优秀人才零星散落着，

cues.en: but not a high density.
cues.zh: 密度没那么高。

cues.en: Remember, I'm about trying to learn how to be great, so I'm studying great people. Bell Labs is a place to study, but the airframe is a place where to get a tool. So I think for a long while, and one day I say to myself, Hamming,
cues.zh: 记住，我一直在琢磨怎么才能变得伟大，所以我在研究那些伟大的人。贝尔实验室是个适合学习的地方，而飞机制造公司则是搞到工具的地方。于是我思索了很久，有一天我对自已说：海明，

cues.en: you believe a machine can do anything.
cues.zh: 你坚信机器能做任何事。

cues.en: Why don't you make the machine do the programming?
cues.zh: 你为什么不让机器来帮我们编程呢？

cues.en: Well, what is the cause? The net effect was that I was put immediately right in the frontier of programming.
cues.zh: 好吧，结果是什么呢？最终的效果是，我一下子被推到了编程的最前沿。

cues.en: How do I make the machine do the programming for us?
cues.zh: 我该怎么让机器替我们编程呢？

cues.en: What appeared to be a defect by turning the problem around became an asset.
cues.zh: 把问题倒过来想，原本看似缺陷的东西反而变成了优势。

cues.en: Grace Hopper has told several other stories a similar way.
cues.zh: 格蕾丝·霍珀也曾用类似的方式讲过好几个故事。

cues.en: What appears to be a defect is an asset.
cues.zh: 看似缺陷的东西，实则是一项资产。

cues.en: So frequently,
cues.zh: 经常地，

cues.en: when you think things are wrong and you haven't got the wherewithal to do it, if you turn the problem around, you can turn it to great success.
cues.zh: 当你觉得事情不对，却没有能力去解决时，如果把问题反过来想，就能把它转化为巨大的成功。

cues.en: Another one is slightly different.
cues.zh: 另一个稍有不同。

cues.en: When I was doing this twenty eighth order system equation I told you about, a navy intercept plane,
cues.zh: 当我在计算我刚才跟你提到的那个 28 阶系统方程时，一架海军拦截机，

cues.en: I was solving it on a digital machine because the analog machine
cues.zh: 我当时是用数字计算机求解的，因为模拟计算机

cues.en: outside of Philadelphia
cues.zh: 费城郊外

cues.en: couldn't do the job. No analog job machine at that day could do it because they didn't have the required accuracy.
cues.zh: 无法完成这项工作。当时没有任何模拟计算机器能够做到这一点，因为它们的精度达不到要求。

cues.en: Well,
cues.zh: 那么，

cues.en: I was using a variation of Mills method which was pretty crummy.
cues.zh: 我当时用的是米尔斯方法的一个变体，效果相当糟糕。

cues.en: I'd had found Mills method was unstable. I patched up a little bit. There it was.
cues.zh: 我发现Mills方法不太稳定，就稍微修补了一下。就这样。

cues.en: One day, I realized the following.
cues.zh: 有一天，我意识到了以下这一点。

cues.en: I was going to have to fill in a report of what I did because government contracts
cues.zh: 我本来还得填一份报告说明我做了什么，因为政府合同

cues.en: always require reports.
cues.zh: 始终要求提供报告。

cues.en: And everybody who had an analog computer was going to try and pick flaws of what I did
cues.zh: 而所有拥有模拟计算机的人，都会来挑我做的东西的毛病。

cues.en: because I was really showing that a digital machine could beat the analog on its own home ground.
cues.zh: 因为我确实展示了数字机器能够在模拟机器的主场战胜它。

cues.en: That's really what I was doing, not getting the answer to the problem. I was really demonstrating something much more important.
cues.zh:
这其实正是我当时在做的事，重点不在于找出问题的答案。

cues.en: I
cues.zh: 我

cues.en: promptly started deriving
cues.zh: 马上开始推导

cues.en: a better method of integrating the differential equations.
cues.zh: 更好的微分方程积分方法。

cues.en: And I finally used method which is for some years was known as Hamming's method. I don't recommend it now, but it was very suitable for the machines as they were.
cues.zh: 我最终用了一种方法，它曾在一段时间里被称为汉明方法。现在我不推荐它，但它非常适合当时那样的机器。

cues.en: And so I had the girl programmer change a few of the instructions,
cues.zh: 所以我让那个女程序员修改了几条指令，

cues.en: run it to check once more to check the new program got the same as the old answers,
cues.zh: 运行一遍再次检查，确保新程序算出的结果和老答案一样，

cues.en: and then went ahead. This report has a very jazzy method of solving
cues.zh: 然后就继续进行了。这份报告用了一种非常时髦的方法来求解

cues.en: differential equations instead of very crummy method.
cues.zh: 微分方程，而不是那种很烂的方法。

cues.en: Both of them equally effective, but one was defensible and one was not.
cues.zh: 两者的效果一样好，但其中一个站得住脚，另一个则不行。

cues.en: You see, changed the nature of the problem. I saw that the problem although originally was get the answers to these trajectories.
cues.zh: 你看，这改变了问题的性质。我发现这个问题虽然最初的目的是算出这些弹道的答案。

cues.en: In fact, it was something else. It was proving that a digital machine could beat the analog machine on its own home ground of differential equations.
cues.zh: 但实际上，它是别的东西。它证明了数字机器能够在微分方程自己的主场上击败模拟机器。

cues.en: I redefined the problem
cues.zh: 我重新定义了这个问题，

cues.en: and made it a success.
cues.zh: 并取得了成功。

cues.en: I would not have found Hamming method if I had not realized that the method I was using, was adequate for me and we could all see we're getting the right answer, but it was not nice. It was not clean and simple. It was rather ugly.
cues.zh: 如果我没有意识到我当时用的那个方法虽然对我来说够用了，大家也都能看出我们得到了正确的答案，但它并不优美，不够干净简洁，反而相当丑陋，我就不会发现 Hamming method。

cues.en: So I changed the problem.
cues.zh: 所以我改变了问题。

cues.en: Now these will all tell you the conditions you want are seldom realized,
cues.zh: 现在，这些都会告诉你，你想要的条件很少能实现，

cues.en: but that you can change the conditions
cues.zh: 但你可以改变这些条件，

cues.en: that you have
cues.zh: 也就是你拥有的条件，

cues.en: to make success.
cues.zh: 来取得成功。

cues.en: Either by inverting the problem or as I told you a second story, changing the nature of problem and recognizing the underlying real problem. Now that's something I've done several times.
cues.zh: 无论是通过反转问题，还是像我刚才讲的第二个故事那样，改变问题的性质并识别出潜在的真正问题。这是我做过好几次的事情。

cues.en: There's one very early problem I solved spectacularly successful,
cues.zh: 有一个很早以前的问题，我解决得极其成功，

cues.en: not only on a computing point of view, but from a physics point of view. The value in the transistor research was extremely valuable.
cues.zh: 不仅从计算的角度来看是如此，从物理学的角度来看也是如此。它在晶体管研究中的价值极其巨大。

cues.en: Well, I meditated over why was that successful.
cues.zh: 嗯，我一直在琢磨为什么会成功。

cues.en: I studied it over and over again.
cues.zh: 我一遍又一遍地研究它。

cues.en: And I believe this statement,
cues.zh: 我相信这样一种说法，

cues.en: you should study your successes.
cues.zh: 你应该去研究你的成功。

cues.en: You don't study your failures.
cues.zh: 不要去研究你的失败。

cues.en: Study successes.
cues.zh: 去研究成功。

cues.en: Because when your time comes, you'll know how to succeed. If you study failures, you'll know how to fail.
cues.zh: 因为当机会来临时，你才知道如何成功；如果你研究失败，你只会知道如何失败。

cues.en: So study success very closely, not only yours, but other people's. Why did Galileo do what he did? How did Newton do it? Try as best you can to study other people. How they succeed? What were the elements of their success?
cues.zh: 所以要仔细研究成功，不仅是你的成功，还有别人的。伽利略为什么要那样做？牛顿是怎么做到的？尽可能去研究别人。他们是如何成功的？他们成功的要素是什么？

cues.en: Which elements of that can you adapt to your personality?
cues.zh: 其中哪些要素是你可以根据自己的个性去调整的？

cues.en: You can't be everybody,
cues.zh: 你不可能成为所有人，

cues.en: but you have to find your own method. And studying success is a very good way of forming your own style.
cues.zh: 但你必须找到自己的方法。而研究成功是形成自己风格的好方法。

cues.en: Now
cues.zh: 现在

cues.en: one day, I think I've told you a story before, I'll be repeating. One day I found John Tookie with whom I was working extensively. He was my age and the guy was clearly a genius.
cues.zh: 有一天——我想我以前给你们讲过这个故事，我要重复一遍——有一天我发现 John Tookie 和我合作得很深入。他和我同龄，而且这人显然是个天才。

cues.en: I went into my... Our mutual boss and says, Henrik,
cues.zh: 我走进我们的共同主管办公室说，Henrik，

cues.en: how can anybody my age know so much as John Tookie does?
cues.zh: 怎么会有人在我这个年纪知道得跟 John Tookie 一样多？

cues.en: Well, he leaned back in his chair, grinned at me and said,
cues.zh: 只见他靠在椅子上，冲我咧嘴一笑说：

cues.en: Hammeh, you'd be surprised how much you'd know if you worked as hard as he did.
cues.zh: Hammeh，如果你能像他那么努力，你也会知道得这么惊人。

cues.en: I slunk out of the office. There wasn't anything to say.
cues.zh: 我灰溜溜地走出了办公室。无话可说。

cues.en: And I stayed home.
cues.zh: 于是我待在家里。

cues.en: When I was home, I thought frequently.
cues.zh: 在家的时候，我经常思考。

cues.en: I'm not working really as hard as I could. I'd never be able to work as hard as John does. I haven't got the psychic energy, but I can work a hell lot harder than I have been.
cues.zh: 我其实并没有竭尽全力去工作。我永远无法像 John 那么拼命，我没有那样的精神精力，但我确实可以比过去努力得多。

cues.en: Let me reorganize my life.
cues.zh: 让我重新规划我的生活。

cues.en: Let me quit spending my time and reading nonsense magazines and coming through the newspaper. They're not very important to my career. Let's spend my time studying things in my career. For example, I got appointed deliberately
cues.zh: 让我别再花时间读无聊杂志、翻报纸了。那些对我的事业并不重要。把时间花在钻研事业相关的东西上。比如，我特意让自己

cues.en: a book review editor. Therefore,
cues.zh: 当上了书评编辑。于是，

cues.en: for... There's always a book on my coffee table right next to waiting to be read and review written.
cues.zh: 我咖啡桌上总放着一本书，等着我去读、去写书评。

cues.en: When a review is written by me, I set aside for a week and ask myself afterwards,
cues.zh: 写完一篇书评后，我会搁置一周，然后问自己：

cues.en: is that a good review? Does that re digest the book? If it doesn't, you're rereading the book and writing a better review.
cues.zh: 这书评写得好吗？真的吃透这本书了吗？如果没有，就重读这本书，写一篇更好的书评。

cues.en: This way, I forced myself to get a lot wide acquaintance
cues.zh: 这样，我强迫自己广泛涉猎

cues.en: in computer science.
cues.zh: 计算机科学领域。

cues.en: And being the book review editor, I got to review the books I wanted.
cues.zh: 而作为书评编辑，我可以评我想评的书。

cues.en: This was a device. Now it's true. I quit reading New Yorker. I quit reading magazines. I quit reading other things. My wife complained occasionally.
cues.zh: 这是个手段。确实如此。我不再读《纽约客》了，不再读杂志了，不再读其他东西了。我妻子偶尔会抱怨。

cues.en: All I looked New Yorker was the jokes.
cues.zh: 我翻《纽约客》只看笑话。

cues.en: She was right.
cues.zh: 她说得对。

cues.en: I didn't have time to do everything. I wasn't a first class genius. I had to work hard.
cues.zh: 我没时间做所有事。我不是一流天才，我必须努力。

cues.en: So I simply set aside those other things and did that.
cues.zh: 所以我就把其他事放一边，专心做那件事。

cues.en: It's not hard to do. You just do it.
cues.zh: 这并不难。你只管去做就行。

cues.en: Now, I wanna say another couple things. The race is not to the swiftest.
cues.zh: 现在，我还想说几点。比赛并不属于跑得最快的人。

cues.en: The guy who works hardest doesn't win. The person who works at the right problem at the right time in the right way is what counts and nothing else.
cues.zh: 最努力的人不一定赢。在正确的时间、用正确的方式、做正确的问题的人，才是关键，别的都不算数。

cues.en: That's what I'm trying to do in this whole course. I've been trying to teach you something about style and taste.
cues.zh: 这就是我这门课一直想做的事。我一直试图教你们一些关于风格和品味的东西。

cues.en: So you'll be able to have some hunch of when the problem is right,
cues.zh: 这样你们就能对什么时候该解决问题、

cues.en: what problem is right, and how to go about it.
cues.zh: 解决什么问题、以及如何解决有一些直觉。

cues.en: The right problem at the right time, the right way counts and nothing else counts.
cues.zh: 在对的时间做对的事，用对的方法，这才是最重要的，其他都不重要。

cues.en: Nothing.
cues.zh: 什么都不重要。

cues.en: You gotta do that.
cues.zh: 你们必须做到这一点。

cues.en: But it's easy. There's a million races being run. You just gotta get in one of them and win.
cues.zh: 但这很简单。有无数场竞赛在进行。你只要加入其中一场并赢得胜利就行了。

cues.en: Now,
cues.zh: 那么，

cues.en: I mentioned earlier
cues.zh: 我刚才提到过

cues.en: regard to the chemist
cues.zh: 关于那个化学家的事情，

cues.en: about
cues.zh: 也就是

cues.en: what are the important problems in your field.
cues.zh: 你所在领域的重要问题是什么。

cues.en: At the urging of some other people partly and partly in my own,
cues.zh: 在别人的部分敦促下，也出于我自己的想法，

cues.en: I used to set aside Friday noon and Friday afternoon for
cues.zh: 我过去常常把周五中午和周五下午的时间留出来，

cues.en: great thoughts.
cues.zh: 用来思考伟大思想。

cues.en: Meaning, yes, I'll answer telephone. Yes, I'll sign a sheet of paper. But mainly,
cues.zh: 意思是，好吧，我会接电话。我会签文件。但主要是，

cues.en: what is the effect of computing on science?
cues.zh: 计算对科学有什么影响？

cues.en: What the hell am I doing with this computing machine?
cues.zh: 我特么到底在用这台计算机搞什么鬼？

cues.en: How is it gonna affect AT and T?
cues.zh: 它将如何影响 AT&T？

cues.en: What should I be doing with computing?
cues.zh: 我应该用计算来做些什么？

cues.en: What is the nature of software?
cues.zh: 软件的本质是什么？

cues.en: My friends all after a while got to know, Friday afternoon's great thoughts.
cues.zh: 过了一段时间，我的朋友们都知道了，周五下午是思考伟大思想的时间。

cues.en: What's the nature of this, that, the other thing?
cues.zh: 这个、那个以及其他事情的本质是什么？

cues.en: I spent 10%
cues.zh: 我花了我 10%

cues.en: of my time trying to answer the question,
cues.zh: 的时间来试图回答这个问题：

cues.en: what are the important problems in my field?
cues.zh: 我领域中重要的问题是什么？

cues.en: Friday afternoon, straight through.
cues.zh: 周五下午，一直持续。

cues.en: Don't do it Monday morning because you'll be interrupted immediately. If you do it Friday afternoon, someone can linger over on the Saturday and Sunday. You do it Monday morning, there's a hot conference at 10:00 and bingo, everything is broken up.
cues.zh: 千万别在周一早上做，因为你马上就会被打断。如果你在周五下午做，有些人的思绪可以延续到周六和周日。如果你在周一早上做，10点钟就会有个紧急会议，啪的一声，全被打断了。

cues.en: I use it Friday afternoon for many, many years. I recommended you find a regular time
cues.zh: 我用了好多年，都在周五下午做这件事。我建议你找一个固定的时间

cues.en: to stop and think.
cues.zh: 停下来思考。

cues.en: What are the important things? What is going on? What is the nature of what you are doing?
cues.zh: 什么是重要的事情？正在发生什么？你所做的事情本质是什么？

cues.en: What is the characteristic of the job?
cues.zh: 这份工作有什么特征？

cues.en: What are the fundamentals behind it? So you have some idea of where you're headed so you can march in a uniform direction and get far rather than being a drunken sailor and getting nowhere.
cues.zh: 背后的基本原理是什么？这样你就能对自己的前进方向有个概念，从而能朝着一个一致的方向走得更远，而不是像个醉酒的水手那样一事无成。

cues.en: And I've regularly this picture tried to stress in his lectures, stress the bigger picture.
cues.zh: 我经常在讲座中试图强调这幅画面，强调更宏大的全局。

cues.en: I've tried to stress fundamentals.
cues.zh: 我一直试图强调基本原理。

cues.en: No one knows what the fundamentals will be tomorrow,
cues.zh: 没有人知道明天的基本原理会是什么，

cues.en: but you can try to ask what are the fundamentals. The things about which other things seem to depend and those things which seem to be true tomorrow, but maybe not.
cues.zh: 但你可以试着去探究什么是基本原理。那些其他事物似乎依赖的东西，以及那些明天看来依然正确、但也可能不正确的东西。

cues.en: I've also stressed the necessity of learning new things.
cues.zh: 我还强调了学习新事物的必要性。

cues.en: All kinds of new fields come up endlessly.
cues.zh: 各种新领域层出不穷。

cues.en: They're gonna keep on coming up. You have to get some grip on them. You can't learn them all, but you have to get an idea. Well, that is relevant to my field. That's interesting, but it isn't relevant. Forget it.
cues.zh: 它们还会不断涌现。你必须掌握它们的一些皮毛。你不可能把它们都学会，但你得有个概念。嗯，这个跟我的领域有关。那个很有趣，但没关系。不用管它。

cues.en: It's a very difficult problem to do.
cues.zh: 这是一个非常难做到的问题。

cues.en: Now there's another thing I have to talk about great people.
cues.zh: 现在我要谈谈另一件事，伟大的人物。

cues.en: Took me a long long while to discover this.
cues.zh: 我花了很长很长的时间才发现这一点。

cues.en: After I've been studying, I would say fifteen or twenty years before I realized
cues.zh: 可以说，我研究了十五或二十年才意识到

cues.en: that tolerance of ambiguity.
cues.zh: 要容忍模糊性。

cues.en: They both believe and disbelieve. Now most people want to believe something is true or isn't true.
cues.zh: 他们既相信，又怀疑。而大多数人非要认定一件事是对还是错。

cues.en: Great scientists believe the theory is true
cues.zh: 伟大的科学家相信理论是对的，

cues.en: enough so they continue working. Because if you don't believe the theory is true, you won't. But they disbelieve enough to notice what's wrong and make the big change to the new theory.
cues.zh: 相信到足以支撑他们继续研究。因为如果你不信它对，就不会做下去。但他们又有足够的怀疑去发现破绽，从而做出重大突破，迈向新理论。

cues.en: If you believe the theory is right,
cues.zh: 如果你坚信这套理论是正确的，

cues.en: you won't make the big change to the next new theory.
cues.zh: 你就不会做出迈向新理论的重大变革。

cues.en: You won't make the big step forward. You'll merely elaborate and extend the old theory.
cues.zh: 你迈不出那一大步。你只会对旧理论修修补补、添砖加瓦。

cues.en: And that won't make you a great scientist. It'll make you just a good one, which I'm not complaining about.
cues.zh: 那成就不了伟大的科学家。顶多算个优秀的，当然这也没什么不好。

cues.en: But
cues.zh: 但是，

cues.en: greatness, it consists of seeing what other people have missed and seizing bond the contradictions
cues.zh: 伟大在于看见别人忽略的东西，抓住矛盾，

cues.en: and making the new step forward.
cues.zh: 并向前迈出全新的一步。

cues.en: You have to tolerate ambiguity. I have not the faintest idea how I'd ever teach a course in ambiguity. I've thought about it many times.
cues.zh: 你必须容忍模棱两可。我完全不知道该怎么开一门讲“模糊性”的课。我想过很多次，

cues.en: How I put a course together to teach students to tolerate ambiguity.
cues.zh: 该怎么设计一门课，去教学生容忍这种不确定性。

cues.en: I haven't a clue.
cues.zh: 我毫无头绪。

cues.en: So I don't know what to do. I'd really tell you that the tolerance of ambiguity, not being so certain everything is correct,
cues.zh: 所以我不知道该怎么教，但我必须告诉你：能够容忍模糊性、不把一切都看得那么绝对，

cues.en: is a necessary feature.
cues.zh: 是一项必备的特质。

cues.en: Now most great scientists have 10 to 20 problems in their minds.
cues.zh: 大多数伟大的科学家脑子里都会装着10到20个问题。

cues.en: Want you to hang around,
cues.zh: 那些一直萦绕在心头的问题，

cues.en: which when they get a clue how to attack, they drop other things and rush you that problem and finish it off first.
cues.zh: 一旦他们找到破解的线索，就会放下别的事，全力扑向那个问题并率先把它攻克。

cues.en: Something between ten and twenty problems which they think important but they don't know what to do. Now let me warn you about important problems.
cues.zh: 大概有十到二十个他们觉得很重要、但又不知道该怎么办的问题。现在我要提醒你们关于重要的问题。

cues.en: Importance is not the consequences.
cues.zh: 重要性并不等于后果。

cues.en: All the time I was at Bell Labs,
cues.zh: 我在贝尔实验室的整个期间，

cues.en: no one worked on the three outstanding problems in physics.
cues.zh: 没有人去研究物理学中那三个未解的难题。

cues.en: Time travel,
cues.zh: 时间旅行，

cues.en: teleportation,
cues.zh: 瞬间移动，

cues.en: and anti gravity.
cues.zh: 还有反重力。

cues.en: They're not important because you haven't got an attack.
cues.zh: 它们之所以不重要，是因为你没有切入点。

cues.en: The importance of a problem to a great extent depends upon have you got a way of attacking the problem.
cues.zh: 一个问题有多重要，很大程度上取决于你有没有办法攻克它。

cues.en: Problems are not important per se, although they have some consequences.
cues.zh: 问题本身并没有那么重要，尽管它们会带来一些后果。

cues.en: The most important thing of... That makes a problem important is that there is an attack. You have an idea how I can go about that problem.
cues.zh: 最重要的事情……让一个问题变得重要的原因，在于有切入点。你得知道我该如何着手解决这个问题。

cues.en: You wanna watch it just because the economic consequences are great and take those three of them, antigravity,
cues.zh: 你不能仅仅因为经济后果巨大就去关注它，比如那三个问题：反重力、

cues.en: teleportation, or time travel.
cues.zh: 瞬间移动，或者时间旅行。

cues.en: The economic consequences are unbelievably large,
cues.zh: 它们的经济影响大到难以置信，

cues.en: but they're not important problems. You have an idea how to do it. When you have, then they may become important.
cues.zh: 但它们并不是重要的问题。你得知道该怎么做。当你知道了，它们或许才会变得重要。

cues.en: Now I've been quite a few times I've been practically saying the following. It is not what you do, it's the way that you do it.
cues.zh: 我有很多次几乎都在说这样的话。重要的不是你做什么，而是你怎样去做。

cues.en: It's the style you go about doing things. It's inverting the problem or changing it. In the words of the song, it ain't what you do, it's the way that you do it.
cues.zh: 这是你做事的方式。是反转问题还是改变问题。正如歌里唱的那样，重要的不是你做什么，而是你怎样去做。

cues.en: It's the style of what you do it. It makes the difference.
cues.zh: 是你做事的方式。这才是关键所在。

cues.en: You only look at special relativity.
cues.zh: 你只关注狭义相对论。

cues.en: Poincare had it all. Some other people had it all before, but Einstein did it the right way. And you only remember Einstein as having done special relativity.
cues.zh: 庞加莱已经全都搞清楚了。其他人之前也都搞清楚了，但爱因斯坦做得最正确。而你只记得爱因斯坦完成了狭义相对论。

cues.en: The other guys had it all. They even give talks on it, but they had a screwed up subject. Didn't have it really clear and straightforward.
cues.zh: 其他人也都搞清楚了。他们甚至还就此做过演讲，但他们的课题搞得一团糟。没有真正清晰直白。

cues.en: Now when you first do a thing, it's often muddled up. And one of your problems is to get it clear so it can be communicated to other people. And you can spend a lot of time lying in bed saying, gee, how can I say that to Joe? If I try it this way, Joe might have misunderstand that. How about that? How about this? Until you finally have a way of looking at a problem which looks simple, straightforward, and clear so you communicate it to others. It may not be the way you found it. It often is not.
cues.zh: 当你第一次做一件事时，往往是一团乱麻。你的问题之一就是把它理清楚，以便能传达给别人。你可以花很多时间躺在床上想，天哪，我怎么跟乔说这个？如果我这样讲，乔可能会误解那个。这样呢？那样呢？直到你最终找到一种看待问题的方式，看起来简单、直白、清晰，能传达给别人。这可能不是你发现它的方式。通常都不是。

cues.en: But getting it clear is important, which brings me to the topic of communication.
cues.zh: 但把它理清楚很重要，这就引出了沟通这个主题。

cues.en: You need to learn to communicate
cues.zh: 你需要学会沟通

cues.en: orally in talks like this,
cues.zh: 像这样在演讲中口头沟通，

cues.en: written in reports,
cues.zh: 在报告中书面沟通，

cues.en: and casual conversations.
cues.zh: 以及日常对话中沟通。

cues.en: In the middle of a conference, have to be able to get up and say, that's wrong for these reasons, bing, bing, bing, bing, and you win.
cues.zh: 在会议中间，你得能站起来说，这是错的，原因如下，砰砰砰砰，然后你就赢了。

cues.en: If you sit around and say, well, I'll write a report tomorrow after I've thought about this some more.
cues.zh: 如果你坐在那里说，好吧，我明天再想想这个，然后写个报告。

cues.en: The decision is made, we go ahead and it doesn't matter what you do then.
cues.zh: 决定已经做了，我们就这么干，那时候你做什么都无所谓了。

cues.en: The ability to communicate is three levels. How do you learn it? You can read books if you want it, but forget it.
cues.zh: 沟通能力有三个层次。你怎么去学呢？你想看书的话倒是可以看，但还是算了吧。

cues.en: The way you learn as far as I'm concerned is every time you go to a talk, you listen not only to talk, but to the style that's done. What talks are effective?
cues.zh: 依我之见，你学习的方式是，每次去听演讲时，不仅要听内容，还要注意它的演讲风格。什么样的演讲才算高效？

cues.en: Why were they effective?
cues.zh: 为什么它们有效？

cues.en: What aspects of the speaker could you adapt?
cues.zh: 演讲者的哪些方面可以调整适配？

cues.en: For example,
cues.zh: 例如，

cues.en: in your... If you're going to give afternoon speeches,
cues.zh: 在你的……如果你要做下午的演讲，

cues.en: generally speaking, there are three jokes. One at the beginning when you get up, one in the middle to keep awake, and one last with a solo remember something that you said.
cues.zh: 一般来说，会有三个段子：开头一个，在你起床时；中间一个，让你保持清醒；最后一个带独奏，记住你说过的话。

cues.en: Well,
cues.zh: 嗯，

cues.en: I had to learn jokes.
cues.zh: 我得学会讲笑话。

cues.en: I discovered that I cannot tell shaggy dog stories.
cues.zh: 我发现自己讲不了那种又长又绕的冷笑话。

cues.en: I can tell one liners very well, but I couldn't. I had to adapt my joke telling to what I could do. Those who told shaggy dog stories, very interesting, I simply cannot do them very well.
cues.zh: 我很会讲一句话笑话，但我做不到。我不得不调整讲笑话的方式，去适应自己能做的。那些讲冗长绕弯故事的人，很有意思，我就是讲不好。

cues.en: You have to adapt what you learn from other speakers to you. When you find a person who's very effective doing something, can you do it?
cues.zh: 你需要把从其他演讲者那里学到的东西应用到自己身上。当你发现某个人的某种做法非常高效时，你能做到吗？

cues.en: Why not?
cues.zh: 为什么不呢？

cues.en: Maybe you can't.
cues.zh: 也许你做不到。

cues.en: Then you have to do something else. But if you yourself will learn to criticize other talks,
cues.zh:
然后你必须做点别的。但如果你自己学会去批判别人的演讲，
@@Ω

cues.en: then you will have a critical basis to criticize
cues.zh: 这样你就有批判的关键基础了

cues.en: your own
cues.zh: 你自己的

cues.en: and then you'll be able to give your talks. If you can only follow what books say instead of learning your own style of creativity,
cues.zh:
然后你就能去演讲了。如果你只能照本宣科，而学不会自己独特的创造风格，
@@
如果只能盲目遵循书本的教条，而无法摸索出属于你自己的创造力风格，

cues.en: it isn't going to work. So I think that the best thing you could do is start
cues.zh: 这行不通。所以我认为你最好的做法是开始

cues.en: as of tomorrow.
cues.zh: 从明天起。

cues.en: When you hear lectures and talks, ask yourself every time, besides what was the content,
cues.zh: 当你听讲座和演讲时，每次都问自己，除了内容是什么，

cues.en: what was a style? What part can I adapt to that technique?
cues.zh: 风格是什么？我可以把哪部分借鉴到那种技巧上？

cues.en: Why was that speech effective? Why is that speech not effective?
cues.zh: 为什么那个演讲有效？为什么那个演讲无效？

cues.en: And you can ask your friends to check that your opinions are somewhat the same with theirs. You may find sometimes they don't agree with you. What's effective talk?
cues.zh: 你可以让朋友核对一下，你的看法是否和他们大致相同。你可能会发现有时他们并不同意你。什么才算有效的演讲？

cues.en: It's a bit of a problem there.
cues.zh: 那有点问题。

cues.en: Now it's a poor workman who blames his tools.
cues.zh: 现在，拙劣的工匠才会怪工具。

cues.en: I've always dropped the philosophy.
cues.zh: 我一直不搞那套哲学。

cues.en: I will do the best I can with what I got.
cues.zh: 我会用现有条件尽力而为。

cues.en: Thus, this school has got a great many faults.
cues.zh: 因此，这所学校有很多缺点。

cues.en: The bureaucracy in Washington does strange things, other things.
cues.zh: 华盛顿的官僚机构会做奇怪的事，还有其他事情。

cues.en: The students have peculiar features they have to disappear now and then.
cues.zh: 学生们有些古怪的特点，他们时不时得消失。

cues.en: Well,
cues.zh: 嗯，

cues.en: you don't blame
cues.zh: 你别怪

cues.en: the system. You do at each course and each lecture the best you can given the circumstances.
cues.zh: 这个系统。在每门课和每场讲座中，你都要在现有情况下尽力而为。

cues.en: This course has suffered from the fact that's being broadcast, so you all been intimidated and afraid just raise your hands and Hamming, I think you're crazy.
cues.zh: 这门课因为被直播而受影响，所以你们都受到威慑，不敢举手说：Hamming，我觉得你疯了。

cues.en: What about such and such?
cues.zh: 那某某事情呢？

cues.en: The fall of this course with the television on is that you people have been too intimidated.
cues.zh: 这门课开着电视的缺点在于，你们这些人太受威慑了。

cues.en: Well, I'll do the best I can. I knew I perfectly well I couldn't get you to interact very actively in a class, so I gave up on that one. Though I did get you one class lecture.
cues.zh: 嗯，我会尽力而为。我完全清楚，我没法让你们在课堂上非常积极地互动，所以我在那一点上放弃了。不过我还是让你们上了一次课堂讲座。

cues.en: Now, there's another thing you have to recognize.
cues.zh: 现在，还有一件你必须认识到的事。

cues.en: If you're going to have progress,
cues.zh: 如果想要取得进步，

cues.en: there has to be change.
cues.zh: 就必须有变革。

cues.en: Change does not mean progress,
cues.zh: 变革并不等同于进步，

cues.en: but progress requires
cues.zh: 但进步需要

cues.en: change.
cues.zh: 变革。

cues.en: Most people and most institutions
cues.zh: 大多数人和大多数机构

cues.en: don't like change.
cues.zh: 都不喜欢变革。

cues.en: They resent it.
cues.zh: 他们对此感到排斥。

cues.en: And therefore, in order to make progress, you have to sort of welcome change.
cues.zh: 因此，为了取得进步，你必须在某种程度上欢迎变革。

cues.en: You have to embrace it despite the fact you don't like it. Why we've all been doing this way perfectly all right now, why should I ever change?
cues.zh: 尽管你并不喜欢它，你也必须拥抱它。为什么我们现在一直用这种完美的方式做事，我为什么要改变？

cues.en: You adopt the model I did.
cues.zh: 你采用了我当时的做法。

cues.en: If the department has been doing this for ten years,
cues.zh: 如果这个部门以这种方式

cues.en: same way, it's time you should change to find out how to do it some other way.
cues.zh: 做了十年，也是时候改变一下，寻找其他做事的方法了。

cues.en: I know it's perfectly satisfactory. Forget it. There might be better methods. You'll never find out if you stay in the same damn rut.
cues.zh: 我知道这已经足够令人满意了。忘掉它吧。可能还有更好的方法。如果你一直陷在老套路里，就永远不会发现。

cues.en: Needless to say, most departments of Bell Labs didn't like my model.
cues.zh: 不用说，贝尔实验室的大多数部门都不喜欢我的模式。

cues.en: But that was my model all the time.
cues.zh: 但这始终是我的模式。

cues.en: If you're doing the same thing for a long while, why is there no other method of doing it better? You will never find other methods if you don't try other things. Some other ones will make them worse occasionally.
cues.zh: 如果你长时间在做同一件事，为什么没有其他更好的方法呢？如果你不尝试别的方法，就永远找不到它们。有些方法偶尔确实会把事情弄得更糟。

cues.en: But without change, you will not have progress.
cues.zh: 但没有变革，就不会有进步。

cues.en: Now when you're learning things I told you, you need to put hooks on ideas so they can recover widely.
cues.zh: 现在，当你学习我告诉你的知识时，你需要给这些想法挂上钩子，以便能够广泛地调取它们。

cues.en: That was the thing that John Took could do and I couldn't for so long.
cues.zh: 这就是约翰·图克能做到而我长期以来做不到的事情。

cues.en: He could dredge up almost any kind of information.
cues.zh: 他几乎能搜寻出任何种类的信息。

cues.en: After he told me, I could see that what he said was true, but I couldn't think of it first.
cues.zh: 在他告诉我之后，我能看出他说的是真的，但我自己先想不出来。

cues.en: So I started doing it either way. I got new piece of information. I turned it around many ways until as it were, it was connected with many piece of information so that in various situations,
cues.zh: 所以我无论如何都开始这样做了。我获取了新的信息。我从各个角度反复琢磨，直到它自然而然地与许多其他信息联系起来，以便在各种情况下，

cues.en: that would come available.
cues.zh: 这些信息都能派上用场。

cues.en: And this has worked out fairly well.
cues.zh: 这种方法效果相当不错。

cues.en: Now you're likely to say to yourself, you haven't got the freedom to work.
cues.zh: 现在你可能会对自己说，你根本没有工作的自由。

cues.en: I didn't either when I began.
cues.zh: 我刚开始时也没有。

cues.en: I had to do more or less what I expected. When you hire a plumber
cues.zh: 我多多少少得做分内的事。当你请一个水管工

cues.en: to fix the plumbing,
cues.zh: 来修理管道时，

cues.en: you expect them to be already trained.
cues.zh: 你期望他们已经受过专业训练。

cues.en: You expect to be able.
cues.zh: 你期望他们能够胜任。

cues.en: You don't give a person a big, lovely chance to do something great when they've not already demonstrated greatness.
cues.zh: 当一个人还没有展现出伟大之处时，你不会给他一个绝佳的机会去成就伟大。

cues.en: The onus is on you to demonstrate greatness and then you'll get the opportunities.
cues.zh: 重任在于你先展现出卓越的能力，然后你才能获得机会。

cues.en: It's not the other way around.
cues.zh: 情况并非倒过来。

cues.en: As beautifully put by an instructor when I was at Nebraska,
cues.zh: 正如我在内布拉斯加州求学时一位导师精辟的话语，

cues.en: The instructor went to head department and said, want to be relieved of some teaching so I can do some research.
cues.zh: 这位导师去找系主任说：“我想减少一些教学工作，以便做点研究。”

cues.en: The head department said, when you've done the research, I'll relieve you the teaching.
cues.zh: 系主任说：“等你做出研究成果了，我就给你减课。”

cues.en: You have to demonstrate your ability first and then you'll have the freedom to do it.
cues.zh: 你必须先证明自己的能力，然后你才有自由去做你想做的事。

cues.en: Otherwise, no. I had to do error correcting codes at home on my own time.
cues.zh: 否则免谈。我不得不利用业余时间在家里研究纠错码。

cues.en: After I became more able, manager left me alone. In fact, at the back end, the management clearly had the belief. The more we left Hamming alone, the more he'd worry about what should be done, more likely he's gonna do the right thing.
cues.zh: 等我能力更强之后，经理就不怎么管我了。事实上，到了后期，管理层显然达成了一种共识：我们越是放手不管 Hamming，让他去操心该做的事，他就越有可能做出正确的选择。

cues.en: That applied to a guy like Hamming who had a conscience and was worried. It doesn't apply to some people. Some people you give them freedom, they'll do nothing.
cues.zh: 这对像汉明这样有良知、会担忧的人适用。对某些人就不适用了。你给有些人自由，他们什么也不做。

cues.en: But I was compulsive and I was worried about doing the right job, so I did.
cues.zh: 但我很有执念，我担心自己做不好该做的事，所以我就去做了。

cues.en: Now I have to ask you a question, is effort
cues.zh: 现在我得问你一个问题：努力

cues.en: to be a great person worth it? Now great is by definition of what you think is great, not mine.
cues.zh: 成为一个伟大的人，值得吗？这里的“伟大”是按你自己认为的伟大来定义的，不是我的定义。

cues.en: Is it worth it? I will claim yes.
cues.zh: 值得吗？我的答案是值得。

cues.en: I've talked to various people. Now people who tried to succeed and didn't, I
cues.zh: 我和各种人聊过。那些努力想成功却没成功的人，我

cues.en: was afraid to ask. But those who did succeed and were famous, I asked them, was the struggle worth? And they said, yep. It's better than wine women and song put together.
cues.zh: 不敢去问。但那些确实成功了、出了名的人，我问过他们：这番奋斗值得吗？他们说，值得。比美酒、女人和歌声加在一起还要好。

cues.en: I didn't ask any women. They might have said better wine, men, and song. I don't know. But they
cues.zh: 我没问过任何女性。她们也许会说是美酒、男人和歌声更好。我不知道。但他们

cues.en: all thought that doing something really first class knowing you've done it is better than anything else they could think of.
cues.zh: 都认为，做成一流的成就、并且知道自己做到了，这比他们能想到的任何事都更好。

cues.en: I can't give you a report of the guys who didn't do it.
cues.zh: 我没法给你那些没做成的人的反馈。

cues.en: As I said, I was afraid to ask them.
cues.zh: 就像我说的，我不敢去问他们。

cues.en: I didn't wanna embarrass them.
cues.zh: 我不想让他们难堪。

cues.en: Well, let me come down now to a saying
cues.zh: 好，现在让我来引用一句话

cues.en: of
cues.zh: 出自

cues.en: Socrates who lived off 470
cues.zh: 苏格拉底，他生活在公元前470年

cues.en: to three ninety nine BC in Greece.
cues.zh: 到公元前399年的希腊。

cues.en: He said,
cues.zh: 他说，

cues.en: the unexamined life is not worth living.
cues.zh: 未经审视的人生不值得过。

cues.en: I heard it while I was cross... First time I heard it while crossing the campus at Yale behind a professor and a student. And the professor turned to the student again and said, the unexamined life is not worth living. And before request, the whole quad, he'd said it three times. The unexamined life is not worth living.
cues.zh: 我是在穿过……第一次听到这句话是在耶鲁校园里穿行，前面有一位教授和一个学生。教授又转向学生说：未经审视的人生不值得过。在走到请求之前，整个方院里，他已经说了三遍。未经审视的人生不值得过。

cues.en: You should examine your life. You've only got one life to lead as far as any of us know.
cues.zh: 你要审视自己的人生。据我们所知，你只有这一辈子可活。

cues.en: Why shouldn't it be the life you want to have instead of whatever happens to you? To come down the back and say, well, I didn't do any harm. I had an enjoyable life.
cues.zh: 为什么不让它成为你想要的生活，而不是任由发生在你身上的一切摆布？到头来回顾一生说，嗯，我没做过什么坏事。我过得挺开心。

cues.en: Is that what you want to say in your old age?
cues.zh: 这就是你年老时想说的话吗？

cues.en: You just had a good time in life?
cues.zh: 你这一生就只是玩得开心？

cues.en: Or do you want to say, you know, I did something that was important, at least something that I thought was important.
cues.zh: 还是你想说，你知道，我做了一些重要的事，至少是我认为重要的事。

cues.en: That's your problem therefore to pick these things up and do it if you want to have a happy life at the back end.
cues.zh: 所以这就是你的问题——如果你想在人生后半程过得幸福，就得把这些事捡起来去做。

cues.en: Now I think all these questions are style I kept saying several times. You've got to work on the right problem at the right time in the right way. Otherwise, you're doomed.
cues.zh: 我觉得这些问题都是风格问题，我反复说过好几次。你必须在正确的时间、用正确的方式、做正确的问题。否则，你就完了。

cues.en: Style is everything and it's not communicable in words. I cannot tell you what makes a great painting. I can show you once. I can show you success which I've done in this class.
cues.zh: 风格就是一切，而且它无法用语言传达。我没办法告诉你什么造就了一幅伟大的画作。我可以给你演示一次。我可以给你展示成功，这门课上我已经这么做了。

cues.en: Now in summary,
cues.zh: 现在总结一下，

cues.en: in a sense, I wanna give you a different view of the whole course, particularly this lecture.
cues.zh: 某种意义上，我想给你们一个关于整门课的不同视角，尤其是这一讲。

cues.en: I'm a revivalist preacher if you want.
cues.zh: 如果你们愿意，可以把我当作一个复兴派布道者。

cues.en: I'm saying, repent your idle ways
cues.zh: 我是在说，忏悔你虚度的光阴吧，

cues.en: and get down and be somebody worth being.
cues.zh: 然后沉下心来，成为一个值得成为的人。

cues.en: This is what this lecture is all about.
cues.zh: 这就是这一讲的全部内容。

cues.en: Revivalist preacher preaching.
cues.zh: 复兴派布道者在讲道。

cues.en: Well, now I've told you things how to succeed.
cues.zh: 好了，现在我已经告诉了你们如何成功的种种。

cues.en: No one ever told me these things I've been telling you.
cues.zh: 从来没有人告诉过我这些我一直以来跟你们讲的事情。

cues.en: Nobody.
cues.zh: 没人。

cues.en: I had to find them for myself.
cues.zh: 我只能自己去寻找答案。

cues.en: I've told you how to succeed.
cues.zh: 我已经告诉你该如何成功了。

cues.en: You have no excuse for not doing better than I did. Thank you.
cues.zh: 你没有任何理由做得比我差。谢谢。
